answers.q1: Inside the `if (!match?.groups)` block, replacing the old `return NaN;`. It runs only when the original single-value regex fails to match, so single-unit inputs take the unchanged path.
answers.q2: `/(-?\d*\.?\d+) *(milliseconds?|msecs?|ms|months?|mo|minutes?|mins?|m|seconds?|secs?|s|hours?|hrs?|h|days?|d|weeks?|w|years?|yrs?|y)(?= *-?\d| *-?\.\d|$)/iy` — flags `i` (case-insensitive) and `y` (sticky); the lookahead requires the component be followed by optional spaces and a number (with optional minus, or a leading '.'), or end of string.
answers.q3: Each matched component (`component[0]`) is passed to the single-value `parse()` recursively and the results are summed. The comment says to keep the single-value parser as the source of unit conversions.
answers.q4: The code records whether the first component's number starts with '-' as `sign`; for each later component, if its negativity differs from `sign`, it returns NaN.
answers.q5: If only one component was consumed (count ≤ 1) it returns NaN (`count > 1 ? total : NaN`). Spaces between components are skipped, but if the string ends with a space after the last component, it returns NaN.
answers.q7: It asserts that `'1' + ' '.repeat(98) + 's'` (100 chars) parses to 1000, and that `'1' + ' '.repeat(99) + 's'` (101 chars) throws. It also checks that an empty string throws.
answers.q8: The README says the `StringValue` type used by `ms` and `parseStrict` describes only single values, so TypeScript users should use `parse` for compound strings.
answers.q9: Type checking (`tsc --noEmit`) was not run because the TypeScript compiler isn't installed in node_modules.
answers.q10: The agent first inspected files, then patched src/index.ts, then added src/compound.test.ts and the README changes in one patch, and then ran `node --test src/compound.test.ts` (alongside git diff check and a tsc check). Only one test run was needed, and all 3 tests passed.

q1.why: Matches: in no-match branch replacing return NaN; only runs when single regex fails.

q2.why: Regex, iy flags, and lookahead all correctly described.

q3.why: Recursive parse on component[0], summed, with the stated reason.

q4.why: First component's '-' sets sign; mismatch returns NaN.

q5.why: Both count>1 requirement and trailing space NaN present.

q8.why: StringValue for ms/parseStrict single values only; use parse.
